differences: Query is dominated by 90.2 Hz with a 30.1 Hz harmonic family, whereas R01 is dominated by 45.9 Hz and has a much broader/noisier spectrum; its full-band Welch distance is also the largest among references.
R01 has strong 4–8 and 8–16 kHz envelope modulation near 61.7/30.9 Hz, while the query has weak 4–8 kHz modulation centered near 182.2 Hz and 8–16 kHz peaks near 90.2/60.2 Hz.
similarities: Both are unclipped 10 s peak-normalized recordings with persistent tonal structure.

differences: R02 is dominated by 45.1 Hz with additional 30.1, 60.1, 75.2 and 90.2 Hz components, whereas the query is dominated by 90.2 Hz and lacks a comparable dominant 45 Hz component.
R02's 100–500 Hz envelope emphasizes 90.2 and 15 Hz and its 4–8 kHz envelope emphasizes 91.7/61.1 Hz; the query instead emphasizes 120.3/90.2 Hz in the low carrier band and 182.2 Hz in 4–8 kHz.
similarities: Both contain a resolved 30.1 Hz-related family and have broadly low-frequency-dominated PSDs.

differences: R03 is dominated by 45.0 Hz and has strong 15 Hz modulation across several carrier bands; the query is dominated by 90.2 Hz and instead has strongest 30.1 Hz modulation in the 500–4000 Hz envelopes.
R03 has broadly high positive filter-bank kurtosis, with median 0.506 and maximum 1.85, while the query is less broadly impulsive despite a localized maximum near 7.5–8.7 kHz.
similarities: Their overall RMS, crest factor and multitaper integrated power are close, and both show approximately 30 Hz harmonic spacing.

differences: R05 is dominated by 43.9 Hz and shows a 29.3 Hz-spaced family; the query is dominated by 90.2 Hz with a 30.1 Hz-spaced family.
R05 has exceptionally strong 29.9–30.0 Hz modulation in the 4–8 kHz band, whereas the query's strongest modulation there is 182.2 Hz and is much weaker.
similarities: Both show approximately 30 Hz repetition and persistent stationary tonal spectra.

differences: Although R06 is the nearest full-band Welch control, R06 is dominated by 44.9 Hz with strong 29.9 Hz content, while the query is dominated by 90.2 Hz.
R06 emphasizes 15 Hz modulation in the 100–500, 1500–4000 and 8000–16000 Hz bands; the query instead emphasizes 120/90 Hz, 30 Hz and 90/60 Hz respectively.
R06 reports numerous level changes, while the query reports none.
similarities: This is the nearest reference in the mean-centered Welch control and also the nearest wavelet signature; both have approximately 30 Hz-spaced harmonic families.

differences: R07 is dominated by 45.9 Hz with additional 76.5 and 30.6 Hz components, whereas the query is dominated by 90.2 Hz with 60.2 and 30.1 Hz components.
R07 has strong 15.3/91.8 Hz low-band modulation, 62.3 Hz modulation at 4–8 kHz and 187 Hz at 8–16 kHz; the query instead has 120.3/90.2 Hz, 182.2 Hz and 90.2/60.2 Hz respectively.
similarities: Both have persistent harmonic spectra and comparable low-order 30–31 Hz spacing evidence.

differences: R08 is dominated by 44.6 Hz with 74.4, 89.3 and 29.8 Hz components, while the query is dominated by 90.2 Hz and has no comparable dominant 44–45 Hz line.
R08 has very strong 30.3/60.6 Hz modulation in 4–8 kHz, whereas the query has much weaker modulation there, led by 182.2 Hz.

The query has a localized spectral-kurtosis maximum of 3.04 near 1060 Hz and filter-bank kurtosis 1.995 near 7.5–8.7 kHz; R08's corresponding maxima are only 0.582 and 0.258. This is evidence of different intermittency, not by itself a fault diagnosis.
similarities: Both show an approximately 30 Hz harmonic family and stationary low-frequency-dominated operation.

decision.explanation: Outcome is different. Initial priorities were the gain-robust Welch/estimator shape, resolved FFT peak families, cross-carrier envelope modulation, and time-frequency persistence; kurtosis and cyclic views were treated as supporting descriptors rather than independent votes. The decisive query evidence is a persistent 90.2 Hz dominant component with a 30.1 Hz-related family and no comparable dominant 44–46 Hz line, while every supplied reference is dominated near 44–46 Hz. The query also has a distinct carrier-dependent modulation pattern and unusually localized intermittency near 1060 Hz and 7.5–8.7 kHz [Q01.C01.S0001, D07.envelope_1, D07.envelope_2, D07.envelope_3, D07.envelope_4, D07.envelope_5, D07.spectral_kurtosis, D07.kurtosis_bank]. Strongest counterevidence is that R06 is the nearest mean-centered Welch control and nearest wavelet control, with R03 also close in overall level and power; however, nearest-reference ranking has no supplied acceptance threshold and conflicts with the resolved frequency and modulation evidence [R06.estimators, R06.wavelet, R06.C01.S0001, R03.estimators, R03.C01.S0001]. Cepstral, cyclic, persistence, reassigned-STFT and wavelet views do not overcome that conflict; their descriptive distances select different references. Orders and synchronous averages are unavailable for the query and every reference because no independent RPM trace was supplied, so no speed-normalized or phase-locked comparison is possible [D07.orders, D07.synchronous, R01.orders, R01.synchronous, R02.orders, R02.synchronous, R03.orders, R03.synchronous, R05.orders, R05.synchronous, R06.orders, R06.synchronous, R07.orders, R07.synchronous, R08.orders, R08.synchronous]. Thus the query is outside the supplied reference set on the strongest resolved evidence; no condition identity, component identity, or severity is supported.
